newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end lower across the board.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end lower across the board.

text.p: All Tokyo corn futures closed lower on Monday, as the yen's strength triggered heavy selling from individual investors, traders said.
Prices were 190 to 310 yen lower, with the benchmark May 1998 contract down 310 yen at 14,590 yen per tonne. The day's volume was 64,386 lots.
Selling from local investors emerged from the opening, traders said. But the price losses were narrower than expected due to the firmer CBOT corn market on Friday, they said.
"We're watching the USDA's crop reports tonight," a brokerage house trader said.

The spot May corn contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $2.93 per bushel at 0825 GMT, up from $2.92 at Friday's close. The spot May of the CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system was at $8.94-3/4 against $8.94-1/4.
